description.text: The Clorox Company is a leading multinational manufacturer and marketer of consumer and professional products with fiscal year 2026 net sales of $6.7 billion and about 9,200 employees worldwide as of June 30, 2026. The Company has operations in approximately 25 countries or territories and sells its products in approximately 95 markets, primarily through mass retailers; grocery outlets; warehouse clubs; dollar stores; home hardware centers; drug, pet and military stores; third-party and owned e-commerce channels; and distributors. Clorox markets some of the most trusted and recognized consumer brand names, including Clorox® cleaning and disinfecting products; Pine-Sol® cleaner; Liquid-Plumr® clog removers; Poett® home care products; Glad® bags and wraps; Fresh Step® cat litter; Kingsford® grilling products; Hidden Valley® dressings, dips, seasonings and sauces; Brita® water-filtration products; and Burt’s Bees® natural personal care products. The Company also markets industry-leading products and technologies for professional customers, including those sold under the Purell®, CloroxPro™ and Clorox Healthcare® brand names. Over 80% of the Company’s sales are generated from brands that hold the No. 1 or No. 2 market share positions in their categories. The Company was founded in Oakland, California, in 1913 and is incorporated in Delaware.

about.description_short: The Clorox Company (NYSE: CLX ) champions people to be well and thrive every single day. Headquartered in Oakland, California since 1913, Clorox integrates sustainability into how it does business. Driven by consumer- centric innovation, the company is committed to delivering clearly superior experiences through its trusted brands including Brita , Burt's Bees, Clorox, Fresh Step, Glad, Hidden Valley, Kingsford , Liquid- Plumr , Pine-Sol and Purell as well as international brands such as Chux , Clorinda and Poett .

analysis_md:
# CLX — The Clorox Company
Pass-1 run, 2026-10-19. Engine 5.5.0. Price $85.63 (nasdaq_quote_api), market cap $10,642,695,810 on 124,287,000 diluted shares — in scope under $40B.

All valuation figures below are copied from dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json or financials_history.csv — none are recomputed. Post-period deal and guidance figures are cited to the company's FY2026 release / 10-K reporting found in research and are context, not valuation inputs.

## What it is
Branded household and professional staples: Clorox bleach and disinfecting cleaning, Glad bags and wraps, Fresh Step cat litter, Kingsford charcoal, Hidden Valley food, Brita filtration, Burt's Bees, plus Purell after the GOJO acquisition closed 2026-04-01. SIC 2842, fiscal year ends June 30. Mature, low-growth categories sold through mass retail; the investment question is durability of cash generation and pricing, not growth.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $981,000,000; capex $220,000,000 (PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment); SBC $81,000,000 (always a real cost).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: $680,000,000 = $5.4712/share.**
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): $1,134,000,000 — above the conservative figure because FY2025 carried a $324,000,000 working-capital release (delta_nwc −$324,000,000 in the CSV); the OCF-based conservative figure is the one used throughout.
- Last 3 FY OE/share: FY2023 $6.9012 (OE $857,000,000), FY2024 $3.2771 (OE $409,000,000), FY2025 $5.4712 (OE $680,000,000). OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years.
- Net debt at FY2025: $2,321,000,000 (cash $167,000,000, total debt $2,488,000,000), plus lease liabilities $392,000,000. That balance sheet predates the two big FY2026 cash deals below — current leverage is materially higher (see HIGH_NET_DEBT).

**Base used = the engine's normalized base, median of the last 3 FY OE/share: $5.4712/share** (base_source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share; the median and the latest FY coincide at $5.4712).

**The TTM base was computed and rejected as the headline base, with reason (ADM / CBRE precedent in this sweep).** ttm.py through 2026-03-31 (ttm.json):
- OCF: FY $981,000,000 − prior YTD $687,000,000 + current YTD $282,000,000 = **TTM $576,000,000**
- Capex: FY $220,000,000 − prior YTD $145,000,000 + current YTD $121,000,000 = **TTM $196,000,000**
- SBC: FY $81,000,000 − prior YTD $64,000,000 + current YTD $49,000,000 = **TTM $66,000,000**
- Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted): **122,240,000**
- **TTM OE total $314,000,000 → TTM OE/share $2.5687**

Why the TTM print is the distorted figure here: the current-YTD OCF leg ($282,000,000 vs $687,000,000 a year earlier) contains the Glad Venture Agreement termination payment — $476,000,000 per the FY2026 10-K cash-flow discussion (research-cited) — paid in January 2026 to acquire P&G's remaining 20% of the Glad business. That is a buyout of a partner's stake in a business Clorox already consolidated, classified in operating cash flow; it is not a recurring cost of selling bleach and bags. The same TTM window also carries the unwind of the ~two weeks of incremental shipments pulled into Q4 FY2025 ahead of the U.S. ERP transition, which management quantifies at about $0.90 of EPS in each direction (inflating FY2025, depressing FY2026). Two honest caveats in the other direction: (1) the median base is FY2025 itself, so it inherits that ~$0.90 ERP pull-forward benefit — the median is flattered, not pristine; (2) the FY2026 full-year release (sales $6.72B, operating cash flow $612,000,000, adjusted EPS $5.53 — research-cited) confirms FY2026 cash generation really was weak even before judging the Glad payment. The verdict does not depend on the choice: on the TTM base a full re-run (moat 6, same scenarios) printed weighted IRR 5.48%, IV@15% $20.42, Tier D (bear 4.26%, bull 6.38%). The median is the more generous defensible base and it still fails the 15% hurdle by a wide margin, so the median stands and the TTM run is the method-range low end.

Data caveat: the FY2026 10-K (period 2026-06-30, filed 2026-08-07) is not yet in EDGAR companyfacts — fundamentals.json states this explicitly — so the engine history stops at FY2025 and the TTM stops at 2026-03-31. FY2026 figures above are from the company's release/10-K reporting, not from the engine's filing-direct history.

## Moat: 6/10 — moderate, durable brands, no growth engine
- FOR: leading category shares across the portfolio (Clorox bleach, Glad, Fresh Step, Kingsford, Hidden Valley, Brita, Burt's Bees — most sales from #1/#2 brands); pricing power proven by the gross-margin rebuild from 35.81% in FY2022 to 45.23% in FY2025 (fundamentals.json annual gross margins: 43.58% FY2021, 35.81% FY2022, 39.36% FY2023, 42.97% FY2024, 45.23% FY2025); ubiquitous retail distribution and household penetration in habitual, low-ticket categories; GOJO/Purell adds a professional hygiene franchise with an installed dispenser base.
- AGAINST: private label plus P&G, Reckitt and Church & Dwight contest largely commoditized categories; no volume growth engine — revenue CAGR 5y 1.11%, 3y −0.01%, latest FY YoY 0.16% (dcf_numbers.json); commodity, manufacturing and logistics inflation repeatedly compresses gross margin (FY2022 trough 35.81%, TTM 43.85%, Q4 FY2026 reported 41.3%); execution shocks (August 2023 cyberattack, the FY2025–26 ERP-transition shipment disruption); post-GOJO/Glad leverage limits flexibility.
- ROIC evidence, as required: fundamentals.json carries **no roic_proxy series for CLX** — the proxy is null for every year because operating income is not tagged separately in the filing facts it reads — and book equity is only $321,000,000 at FY2025 after years of buybacks and dividends, so neither a filed ROIC history nor ROE can evidence returns above the cost of capital. The 6 therefore rests on brand share, distribution and the demonstrated pricing recovery, and is not raised to 7+ without that measured ROIC evidence.
- A 6 gives CAP = 9.8 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 9.8 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — final run (2026-10-19)
Engine blended growth g_base is −0.03%: revenue CAGR 5y 1.11%, 3y −0.01%, latest YoY 0.16%, OE/share CAGR 2y −10.95% (that leg runs FY2023's impairment-era $6.9012 to FY2025's $5.4712 and is a level effect, not a trend). Default offsets and OE multipliers retained; probabilities default 10/25/30/25/10.

**Growth-start sanity check (mandatory):** the base start of −0.03% sits below FY2027 organic sales guidance of +3.5% to +4.5% — written reason: management states more than 3.5 points of that organic guide is the mechanical lap of the FY2026 ERP inventory drawdown, so underlying organic growth is roughly 0–1%, and FY2027 also carries guided cost inflation (more than $200M, front-loaded) with gross margin guided to about 42% vs 45.23% in FY2025, so OE growth lags sales. The bull start (+4.97%) sits at the top of the organic guide plus a full year of GOJO; the super-bull start (+11.97%) is in line with guided *reported* FY2027 sales growth of 13% to 14%, which is acquisition-driven (about 9.5 points from GOJO), not organic — it is credited only at 10% probability. Bear (−5.03%) and super bear (−10.00%, the engine floor) mirror the FY2026 experience: reported sales fell about 5% in FY2026 with gross margin down sharply in Q4.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 10% | −10.00% | 0.75 | $19.33 | 4.82% |
| Bear | 25% | −5.03% | 0.90 | $28.89 | 6.36% |
| Base | 30% | −0.03% | 1.00 | $40.08 | 8.23% |
| Bull | 25% | 4.97% | 1.10 | $55.08 | 10.64% |
| Super bull | 10% | 11.97% | 1.25 | $85.43 | 14.97% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $43.49 (−49.2% vs the $85.63 price), IV@20% $31.08, IV@25% $24.19, weighted IRR 8.85%.**
- **Tier by numbers: D.** Bear tier D (6.36%), bull tier C (10.64%). Diagnostics (dcf_numbers.json): OE yield 6.39%, terminal value 17.8% of IV@15%, scenario spread 4.42x, net debt 3.41x normalized OE, 15.6 months since FY end.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest fiscal year ended 15.6 months ago): ttm.py was run and its legs are quoted in full above. The TTM base was not adopted for the reason stated there — its current-YTD OCF leg contains the $476,000,000 Glad Venture Agreement termination payment and the ERP drawdown unwind — and the TTM re-run is carried as the method-range low end (weighted IRR 5.48%, Tier D). Separately, the FY2026 10-K is filed (2026-08-07) but not yet in EDGAR companyfacts (fundamentals.json note), so no filing-direct FY2026 base exists for the engine to use.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (net income vs OCF differ by >40% in 2023, 2024): the one-offs are in net income, not in the OCF base. FY2023: net income $149,000,000 vs OCF $1,158,000,000 (financials_history.csv) — the 10-K income statement carries $445,000,000 of goodwill, trademark and other asset impairments in FY2023 (the VMS business), a non-cash charge that depresses net income without touching operating cash flow. FY2024: net income $280,000,000 vs OCF $695,000,000 — the same statement carries a $240,000,000 loss on divestiture and a $171,000,000 pension settlement charge in FY2024, again largely non-cash/divestiture items, in the cyberattack recovery year. Resolution: the divergence is explained by non-cash charges against net income; the conservative OE base is built from OCF, so it is not flattered or depressed by them.
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (super-bull IV 4.42x super-bear IV): real — the range runs from a levered, flat staples compounder in decline to an acquisition-assisted recovery. Confidence is capped below high (set to low, given the base-choice spread and the post-period leverage change), and the verdict is sized to the bear end.
- **HIGH_NET_DEBT** (net debt 3.41x normalized OE): balance sheet from the filing (financials_history.csv, FY2025): cash $167,000,000, total debt $2,488,000,000, net debt $2,321,000,000, lease liabilities $392,000,000, equity only $321,000,000. That is the *pre-deal* picture: in FY2026 Clorox paid the $476,000,000 Glad termination amount (January 2026) and closed the GOJO acquisition on 2026-04-01 (a $2.25B deal per research-cited reporting), both debt-funded — Q3 FY2026 reporting already showed cash of $1,187,000,000 raised against long-term debt of $2,487,000,000 at 2026-03-31, before the GOJO close. Pro-forma leverage is therefore materially above the filed 3.41x, the FY2026 free cash flow of the business did not cover its dividend (release-era reporting), and the bear/super-bear OE multipliers (0.90 / 0.75) are where that stress is carried.
- **TIER_BAND** (bear D 6.36% vs bull C 10.64%): the verdict is sized to the bear end — final tier D. Both ends of the band sit below the 15% hurdle, so the band changes the margin of failure, not the conclusion.

## Thoughts / method range
- Method range: median base $5.4712 → weighted IRR 8.85%, IV@15% $43.49, Tier D; TTM base $2.5687 → weighted IRR 5.48%, IV@15% $20.42, Tier D. A normalized base that also stripped the ~$0.90 ERP pull-forward benefit out of FY2025 would land between the two. Every defensible base is Tier D at $85.63.
- The business itself is not broken: OE was positive in all of the last 5 fiscal years, gross margin was rebuilt to 45.23% by FY2025, and FY2027 guidance implies adjusted EPS growth off the depressed FY2026 print. The problem is price versus growth: a flat-revenue staples franchise at $85.63 needs sustained mid-single-digit OE growth to clear 15%, and neither the last five years (revenue CAGR 1.11%) nor underlying guidance (roughly 0–1% organic ex-lap) supplies it.
- Watch items: whether GOJO/Purell and full Glad ownership convert into OE rather than just reported sales; gross margin against the guided ~42% and the $200M+ cost inflation; debt paydown from FY2027 cash flow versus the dividend; the September 2026 voluntary recall of roughly 6.3M units (research-cited) as a brand/quality signal.
- Hurdle prices (dcf_numbers.json): clears 15% below $43.49, 20% below $31.08, 25% below $24.19.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: D** (weighted IRR 8.85% on the median base; 5.48% on the TTM base — D on both)
- Confidence: **Low** (on the precision of the IRR, given the $2.5687–$5.4712 base spread, the wide scenario spread, and leverage that stepped up after the filed balance sheet; the narrower claim that $85.63 does not clear 15% holds on every base tried)
- One-liner: Durable branded staples franchise, moat 6/10, but flat growth, a one-off-depressed TTM and rising post-deal leverage leave weighted IRR at 8.8% — it clears 15% only below $43.49 vs the $85.63 price.
